chosen.premise: Raticate uses whiskers for balance, slows down without them, and bites anyone who touches them.
chosen.hook: Touch this Pokémon’s whiskers, and it will bite you.
chosen.visualIdea: A running Raticate tilts off-balance as whiskers vanish, then snaps at a hand reaching toward them.
chosen.note: A very Raticate-specific contradiction: delicate whiskers are essential for balance, yet touching them triggers a bite. Every part of the premise is directly supported.

candidates.premise: Raticate’s webbed hind feet let it cross rivers—and it can sometimes swim across oceans.
candidates.hook: Why does a Normal-type mouse have flippers?
candidates.visualIdea: Close-up of tiny webbed rear feet transforms into flippers as Raticate swims from a river to open ocean.
candidates.note: The ocean-crossing mouse is an excellent visual surprise and explicitly supported, though the webbed-feet premise is slightly less exclusive to Raticate than the whisker mechanic.

candidates.premise: Alolan Raticate weighs 25.5 kg, but its Totem form is twice as tall and weighs 105 kg.
candidates.hook: This Raticate becomes twice as tall—and over four times heavier.
candidates.visualIdea: Standard and Alolan Raticate stand beside a scale, then Totem Alola rises to 1.4 m as 105 kg slams onscreen.
candidates.note: The measurements create a clear, memorable transformation: 0.7 m to 1.4 m and 25.5 kg to 105 kg. Strong data-driven angle, though it depends on variant comparison rather than core Raticate biology.

candidates.premise: Raticate’s ever-growing fangs force it to gnaw constantly—and can even topple concrete buildings.
candidates.hook: This mouse has to chew concrete so its teeth don’t outgrow its face.
candidates.visualIdea: Fangs grow like a meter, then Raticate rapidly chews rocks, logs, a house wall, and a concrete building.
candidates.note: The concrete-chewing claim is strongly supported and highly visual, but “gnaw constantly” overstates the entries, which say the fangs grow steadily and require grinding down.

candidates.premise: Raticate looks harmless, but its bite can cleanly take off a hand.
candidates.hook: Do not judge Raticate by its face.
candidates.visualIdea: Cute official art gets a sweet introduction before warning labels, huge fangs, and a hand pulling away fast.
candidates.note: The hand-biting warning is directly supported, but “looks harmless” is subjective and the angle overlaps with the more specific whisker-biting mechanic.

candidates.premise: Rattata evolves at level 20 into a 0.7 m Raticate whose fangs can chew apart cinder walls.
candidates.hook: At level 20, this tiny rat evolves into a wall-chewer.
candidates.visualIdea: Level 19 Rattata hits level 20, evolves in a flash, then Raticate bites through a cinder-block wall.
candidates.note: The level-20 trigger and cinder-wall payoff are concrete and filmable, but the evolution method is secondary-source data and the angle combines game progression with Pokédex lore.

rounds.request: Not applicable; the whisker-balance-and-bite angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally Raticate-specific mechanic, a directly supported contradiction or number, and a clear visual payoff.
